body:
Entitlements per-se do not allocate any native memory, and have a small heap footprint. However, their implementation relies on class transformation to inject bytecode that checks the caller actions against its policy. We use [java.lang.instrumentation](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/24/docs/api/java.instrument/java/lang/instrument/package-summary.html) classes to perform that; instrumentation in turn uses  the native [jvmti](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/24/docs/specs/jvmti.html), at least in _some_ cases (for sure, re-transformation of already loaded classes).

The current hypothesis is that re-tranformation (and maybe even transformation) makes the JVM (jvmti) retain some data structures in its internal memory (maybe even the whole un-transformed class bytecodes?), leading to the ~100MB of "Internal" space increase.

We only instrument about 56 classes, so this is around 2MB per class. This seems like an absurd amount of memory. I have a hunch something [accidentally quadratic](https://www.tumblr.com/accidentallyquadratic) is going on.

issue.title: Return null from transformer when not transforming

issue.body:
The transform API for instrumentation should return null when no transformation occurs. This commit fixes our entitlement transformer to return null instead of the original buffer.

closes #125920
